title: BOX OF MID-CENTURY FILM POSTER...
reason: Under-described box with several 1950s Marilyn Monroe lobby cards (Niagara, Bus Stop and others); if the cards are originals the lot could reach a few hundred dollars, but the modern portrait prints and possible reprints cap it.
findings: Box of roughly 15 to 20 loose film and star items, mostly Marilyn Monroe, which the title does not name. Photo 1 shows US-style 11x14 lobby cards: NIAGARA (Technicolor, 'Marilyn Monroe, Joseph Cotten, Jean Peters', black side panel with the Fox logo, teal script title) and BUS STOP (yellow card, 'Marilyn Monroe', 'Don Murray', CinemaScope). Photo 7 is THE GIRL CAN'T HELP IT (20th Century-Fox, Tom Ewell, Jayne Mansfield, Edmond O'Brien, CinemaScope, Color by De Luxe, full credits legible). Partly hidden in photo 1: a red and white dancer-title card (title unreadable, possibly a Marilyn musical), a black 'Tom Ewell' CinemaScope card (possibly The Seven Year Itch, unconfirmed), a CAPE FEAR card with the yellow splat logo, a green card with 'O'Brien', and a loose cut-out of a man in a peaked cap and sunglasses (looks like MacArthur) with a strip of tape on it. Photo 3 is a pink-toned, faded costume-drama still or card (not identified). Photo 4 is a 'New Screen News' cover dated April 28, 1950 (Virginia Mayo, Warner Bros star, price 3d). Photos 2, 5 and 6 are glossy portraits: a colour smiling portrait in a clear sleeve and two black-and-white Marilyn prints (one holding a fan of play money, one in a white fur stole with drop earrings) that look like modern posters or digital prints, not period photographs; there is also a 'Marilyn Monroe' headed book or poster. Authenticity of the cards cannot be judged from 800x600 photos: the Bus Stop card looks properly aged, the Niagara card is crisp with clean borders (could be an original or a reprint), and no NSS numbers or fine print could be read.
condition: Cards look mostly flat with light edge wear. Bus Stop card has toned edges and foxing along the top. The pink-toned still is faded with a surface mark. Some prints are in clear sleeves with creasing, and the MacArthur cut-out has tape on it. Pieces overlap, so the lower items cannot be assessed.
rescore_note: Likely a mix of period Fox lobby cards (Niagara scene card, Bus Stop, probable Seven Year Itch, Girl Can't Help It, Cape Fear) plus modern Monroe prints and a loose cut-out; if the main cards are originals the lot is worth roughly AU$200 to $400, but a Niagara title card (the premium card of that set) made only US$275 (RR Auction, 15/08/2019, https://www.rrauction.com/auctions/lot-detail/341565105649498-marilyn-monroe-niagara-title-lobby-card/) and 20 mixed Monroe cards made US$1,875, about US$94 each (same sale, https://www.rrauction.com/auctions/lot-detail/li/341570205649504/cat/0), and authenticity cannot be judged from the photos, so the realistic mix of genuine and reprint is about AU$150 to $250.
